newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares end week firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares end week firmer.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrials closed firmer on Friday, thriving on initial positive market sentiment towards an annual national budget unveiled on Thursday, brokers said.
The key index jumped 185.31 points on Friday to close at 11,469.98 and was 63.53 points firmer on the week.

"Early analysis indicates that the budget will be positive for the stock market," one broker said, pointing as one example to a new tax to be levied on interest earned on treasury bills from next January, which he said might drive investors from the local money market to the bourse.

Another market analyst on Thursday said finance minister Herber Murerwa's optimism over Zimbabwe's prospects of securing a resumption of Western donor aid for further economic reforms suspended in 1995 over fiscal overspending would also boost sentiment on the market.
The day's advances were in house appliance maker Capri which surged 220 cents to 400 while cigarette firm Rothmans climbed 200 cents to 4,500.
Blue chip Delta, cement group Porthold and pharmaceutical company Caps all added 100 cents to 2,100, 2,300 and 3,100 respectively and bankers NMB were up 50 cents to 3,600.

Minings continued lustreless with most counters trading unchanged from previous levels while coal producer Wankie put on 20 cents to 610. The seven-share index there rose 7.48 points to 792.87, but lost 47.31 points during the week.
